Dear Mr Shepherd
| refer to your employment as an Administration Officer (AO), Switchboard Operations - Corporate
Services, Logan Hospital (LH), Metro South Health (MSH). | write to you in relation to concerns
raised regarding your workplace behaviour and conduct.
Background
On 14 April 2025, following a team meeting, Ms Chloe Taylor, Switchboard Manager, Switchboard
Operations, LH, MSH and Ms Sonya Willmann, Telecommunications Coordinator, Switchboard
Operations, LH, MSH, met with you to remind you of the process for absence notifications under
the LH Switchboard Sick Leave Process (Attachment 1). This conversation was raised on the
basis that you were not following the appropriate absence notification process. Ms Taylor
summarised the discussion of this meeting with you via email (Attachment 2).
Since this meeting, you have failed to adhere to the process on the following fourteen (14)
occasions:

1. On 17 April 2025, you called Ms Taylor at 13:01 advising you will be late to your 14:00
shift. You sent a text message at 13:53 advising that you were still at the mediation, and
you would be taking leave without pay as you had not left yet (Attachment 3).

2. On 23 April 2025, you emailed Ms Wilmann at 05:14 requesting urgent leave for the day
to prepare for a personal hearing scheduled for 28 April 2025. Your shift was due to
commence at 06:00 (Attachment 4a). Ms Taylor sent you a text message at 06:26
confirming if you were working as you were rostered from 06:00. You responded and
advised that you thought Ms Wilmann was on call and that you emailed her to confirm your
absence. (Attachment 4b).

3. On 24 April 2025, you called Ms Wilmann at 05:54 advising you could not attend your shift
and apologised for the short notice. Your shift was due to commence at 6:00 (Attachment
5).

4. On 28 April 2025, you sent a text message to Ms Willmann at 00:29 advising you would
not be in for your 06:00-14:00 due to personal matters. You were not rostered to work this
day (Attachment 6).

5. On 30 April 2025, Ms Taylor contacted you when she arrived at work at 07:30. You advised
that you had slept in and were on your way to work. At 07:48 you sent a text message to
state that your phone was not working, and you were taking it in to get it fixed and you will
not be attending your shift (Attachment 7).
6. On 1 May 20285, you sent an email to Ms Taylor at 06:16 stating you had a large infection
and would not be in for your 07:00 — 15:00 shift. Your phone had not been fixed
(Attachment 8).

7. On 2 May 2025, the switchboard contacted you at 06:10 as you did not arrive for your 06:00
shift commencement. You advised that you would not be coming in and that you sent a text
message to Ms Taylor confirming your absence. You messaged Ms Taylor at 6:15 to advise
that you would not be in for your 06:00 — 14:00 shift because you were unwell (Attachment
9). Ms Taylor received a medical certificate from you at 09:25 via email

8. On 4 May 2025, Ms Taylor contacted you to confirm your attendance for your shift from
06:00 — 14:00. You responded that you did not review the roster properly and were not
aware that you were rostered to work (Attachment 10). You did not perform this rostered
shift.

9. On 13 May 2025, you sent a text message at 02:10 to the personal mobile of Ms Willmann
advising that you were in pain and would not be attending your shift in the morning
(Attachment 11).

10. On 15 May 2025, you contacted Ms Kaymarie Court, Administration Officer, Switchboard
Operations, LH, MSH, on her personal mobile at 14:40 advising that you would be 10
minutes late for the commencement of your shift at 15:00. At 15:30 you had still not arrived
for your shift (Attachment 12).

11. On 17 May 2025, you sent a text message to Ms Willmann on her personal mobile at 05:33
advising that you were not well and would not be attending your rostered shift between
06:00 — 14:00. (Attachment 13).

12. On 26 May 2025, you sent a text message to Ms Willmann on her personal mobile at 23:05
advising of your absence for your rostered shift at 06:00 — 14:00, the following day
(Attachment 14).

13. On 28 May 2025, you sent a text at 05:00 that you would need to take extra time off in the
morning (first part of rostered shift) but could attend the second half of the shift. You were
advised that due to limited resources, your entire shift would require filling and not part.
This shift was covered on your behalf. (Attachment 15a and Attachment 15b).

14. On 29 May 2025, you called Ms Willmann to state that you would be 15 minutes late
(Attachment 16). You also advised you needed to leave work at 12:00 to sign paperwork.
You contacted Ms Taylor at 07:18 to confirm if she was at work as your swipe card was not

working and you could not get in to work

On 10 June 2025, Ms Taylor met with you to remind you of the process for absence notifications
under the LH Switchboard Sick Leave Process. Ms Taylor reminded you to not message/contact
staff directly when running late and to call switchboard to be transferred to the manager on duty to
advise of the delay. Ms Taylor also discussed the inconsistency of the communication being sent
by you in making contact after hours for non-urgent matters and providing limited notice of absence
before a shift commencement time. A copy of the process was provided to you at this time for your
reference. Ms Taylor summarised the discussion of this meeting with you via email (Attachment
17)

Since this meeting whereby you were reminded of the process, you have failed to adhere to the
process on the following four (4) occasions:

1. On 22 June 2025, you sent a text message to the on-call mobile at 09:32 advising that you
had personal things and were late to work. You were rostered to commence work at 07:00
(Attachment 18a).

2. On 22 June 2025, you sent a text message to the on-call mobile at 22:21 requesting the
day off for the next day because your car had been stolen. You were rostered to work 07:00
— 15:00 (Attachment 18b).

3. On 23 June 2025, you sent a text message to the on-call mobile at 21:30 requesting the
next day off and that you would be back on Wednesday (Attachment 19).

4. On 25 June 2025, you called Ms Taylor’s personal mobile at 13:55 advising that you would
be late for your 14:00 shift (Attachment 20). You arrived for your rostered shift at 14:27.

On 25 June 2025, you attended a meeting with Ms Taylor to discuss the process for notifying of
unplanned absences. During this meeting, Ms Taylor reminded you of the requirement to following
the on-call procedure and not message/contact staff directly when running late and to either call
herself or switchboard in order to be transferred to the manager on duty to advise of the delay and
the requirement for leave forms to be submitted as soon as possible following an absence to ensure
correct wages were paid. You were provided with a further copy of the on-call procedure for your
reference. Ms Taylor summarised the discussion of this meeting with you via email (Attachment
21).

Since this meeting, you have again failed to adhere to the process on the following sixteen (16)
occasions:

1. On 1 July 2025, you were rostered 06:00 to 14:00 however departed your shift early at
12:00 noon citing personal matters and fatigue due to relocating to Brisbane. You submitted
a request in MyHR to access fatigue leave, which was declined on the grounds that the
‘fatigue’ experienced was due to personal circumstances and not work related.

2. On 9 July 2025, you sent a text to Ms Wilmann at 06:52 stating that you would be late for
your shift that was to commence at 07:00 due to family issues overnight and you anticipated
arriving at 07:30. Ms Taylor received a call from switchboard staff to advise that you had not
arrived at 07:40. Ms Taylor sent you a text message requesting you confirm when you had
arrived to work. You advised that you had to get a coffee from McDonald's, park the car and
then you would be in. You confirmed arrival for your shift at 08:30.

3. On 10 July 2025, you were rostered to work 07:00 — 15:00, however commenced your shift
at 08:00. You did not advise the supervisor on duty that you were late, and the roster was
not updated to reflect this. Ms Taylor emailed you on 14 July 2025; to confirm the reason
for your lateness and understand why you failed to notify a leader of your change in shift
time. To date, you have failed to provide Ms Taylor with a response.

4. On 16 July 2025, you sent a text at 14:58 advising you would be late for your 15:00 - 23:00
shift. You arrived to work at 15:30.

5. On19 July 2025, you were rostered to work 15:00 — 23:00. You called 16:30 to advise you
had slept in.

6. OMm24duly2025y;you sent a text message at 12:37pm and advised you would be unable to
attend your 14:00 shift due to court.

7. On1 August 2025, during your shift (06:00-14:00) you approach Ms Taylor at approximately
09:00 to advise that you had won your court case, and you had to leave to collect your dog.
There was a meeting scheduled with you, Ms Taylor and | at 10:00 to gain more clarity into
your court attendances and address our concerns with your attendance. This meeting was
rescheduled.

8. On 4 August 2025, you sent a text message at 1033 advising that you were at the
courthouse and unable to attend your 12:00 — 20:00 shift. The 12:00 meeting with you, Ms
Taylor and | was rescheduled.

9. On 5 August 2025, you sent a text message at 9:19 to Ms Taylor stating that you were
unable to attend your 12:00 — 20:00 shift. You did not provide a reason for your absence.
The 12:30 meeting with you, Ms Taylor and I was rescheduled.

10. On 6 August 2025, you sent text message at 14:04 to Ms Taylor advising that you were
unable to attend your 14:00 shift as your phone died and your dog couldn't be located to be
picked up yet. Your 14:00 meeting with Ms Taylor and | was rescheduled.

11. On 7 August 2025, you called Ms Taylor at 14:50 to advise that you were going to be late
for your 1500 shift. You arrived at 15:30. Your meeting was scheduled for 15:00 with Ms
Taylor and me. You enquired why the meeting was scheduled and requested a union
representative be present for the meeting. The meeting was rescheduled.

12. On 11 August 2025, you sent a text message to Ms Taylor at 18:47 to advise that you could
not work 12, 13 and 15 August but could work night shifts. Ms Taylor clarified that your
rostered shifts were for the 12, 13 and 14 August 2025 and requested that you provide an
email outlining the reason for your absence. You failed to respond to Ms Taylor.

13. On 13 August 2025, Ms Taylor contacted you again to confirm your availability to work your
shift on 13 August 2025.

14. On 13 August 2025, you sent a text message to confirm you will be sending an email
tonight. You advised you were in session pleading your case and would be at work the next
day 14:00 — 22:00.

15. On 14 August 2025, you sent a text message at 10:45 stating that you were sorry for the
late response and needed the day off. You advised that you forward the email that day. You
were rostered to work 14:00 — 22:00.

16. On 17 August 2025, Switchboard contacted Ms Taylor to advise that you had not arrived
for your 16:00 — 14:00 shift. Ms Taylor sent you a text message at 06:17 and you responded
to advise that you thought you were working from 07:00-15:00. You had looked at the next
fortnights roster. You advised that you were 20 minutes away from work, however arrived
at 07:15 for your shift.

Reminder of expectations

| do acknowledge that you are currently experiencing some challenging personal matters but it is
important for you to be aware that the expectation remains for you to meet the professional
standards required of you in your role as an Administration Officer and as an employee of MSH.
Personal difficulties, while understandably impactful, do not exempt employees from fulfilling core
responsibilities, including those related to attendance and communication.

It concerns me that since initially being reminded by Ms Taylor on 14 April 2025, of the expectations
for you to follow the LB Switchboard Sick Leave process, you have failed to follow this process for
a total of thirty-four (34) occasions.

To address these concerns with you and put in strategies to support and assist and improvement,
| have attempted to arrange to meet with you on a number of occasions. However, these meetings
have not taken»place due:to. you. not being. inthe werkplace.

Next Steps

| am very concerned about the ongoing impact your frequent absences and/or late attendance for
rostered shifts are having on Switchboard Services and the overall service delivery to Logan
Hospital.

Given the ongoing nature of these attendance issues and non-adherence with the LB Switchboard
Sick Leave process, Ms Taylor will organise a meeting with you to discuss options to assist you in
both improving your attendance and your compliance with the appropriate processes in place, along
with reviewing and updating your PDP.

You will be provided the opportunity to have a support person of your choosing to this meeting. |
encourage you to work collaboratively with Ms Taylor throughout this process so that we can
provide the necessary support to help you succeed in your role and contribute effectively to the
team and service delivery.

| must advise you; Ms Taylor and | are committed to you and considering any strategies to assist in
your improvement. However, it is important to note if there is not an improvement or if you continue
to fail to follow the processes in place, this may be grounds to consider initiating a Performance
Improvement Plan (PIP) focused specifically on addressing absenteeism, punctuality and
compliance with all relevant policies and procedures in place relating to attendance.

Frequent absences and late arrivals disrupt workflows, place additional strain on your colleagues,
and can ultimately compromise the quality and timeliness of service delivery to patients and the
wider community. Immediate and sustained improvement in your attendance is therefore crucial to
uphold the standards expected of MSH and to ensure uninterrupted support to Logan Hospital.
Moving forward, | expect you to familiarise yourself with the process for absence notification in
Switchboard Services and ensure you adhere to these steps consistently. Should you require time
off to manage your personal situation, please reach out to Ms Taylor to discuss available support
options and leave arrangements.

Page 4 of 5 Metro South Health
| would also like to take this opportunity to remind you of your responsibility to act professionally
and meet your obligations as an employee of Queensland Health. This includes the responsibilities
imposed on you by the Code of Conduct for the Queensland Public Sector (the Code of Conduct)
(attached) and our MSH Values (attached).

Direction to undertake training

Prior to your meeting with Ms Taylor, you are required to undertake the following actions:

e read the process for absence notification in Switchboard Services
e sign attached acknowledgement confirming you understand the requirements of the process
and return within seven (7) calendar days from receipt to Ms Taylor.

Employee assistance

| acknowledge this may be a difficult time for you. | would like to take this opportunity to also advise
you of the Employee Assistance Program. This is a confidential counselling service which is free of
charge to all employees of MSH for up to six sessions per calendar year. Access to this service is
by self-referral. Should you wish to access Employee Assistance, please contact TELUS Health on
1800 604 640 or for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander support, please contact TELUS Health on
1800 816 152.

Questions

If you have any questions in relation to the matters in this letter, please do not hesitate to get in
contact with Ms Chloe Taylor, Manager, Logan and Beaudesert Health Service on (07) 2891 5906
or via email at LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au.

Yours sincerely

Scott Hughes

Director

Corporate Services
